sentences.en: Medellín, Colombia is set in the middle of a steep valley of green mountains with a river running through the middle.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚的麦德林坐落在绿树成荫的陡峭山谷中央，一条河流从中穿城而过。

sentences.en: In this busy city of about 4 million people, the weather is perfect, averaging about 72 degrees Fahrenheit year-round.
sentences.zh: 在这个拥有约四百万人口的繁忙城市里，天气好得不得了，全年平均气温在72华氏度左右。

sentences.en: We call it La Ciudad de la Eterna Primavera, the city of eternal spring.
sentences.zh: 我们叫它“永恒的春天之城”。

sentences.en: It's both urban and forested, and it's just a beautiful place.
sentences.zh: 这里既有都市风情，又充满绿意，实在是个美丽的地方。

sentences.en: I spent some of my childhood there.
sentences.zh: 我的童年有一部分是在那里度过的。
说话的是制作人路易斯·加洛。

sentences.en: I remember afternoons at my aunt's apartment way up in the hills of Medellín.
sentences.zh: 我记得在麦德林群山深处我阿姨的公寓里度过的那些下午。

sentences.en: She'd teach my cousin, my brother, and me how to paint.
sentences.zh: 她会教我和堂弟、还有我弟弟画画。

sentences.en: And from her windows, I could see the whole city, the high-rise towers dotting the forested valley.
sentences.zh: 从她的窗户望出去，我能看到整座城市，高层建筑点缀在绿树环抱的山谷中。

sentences.en: I can still smell the air, a mix of pine and balsa trees, and damp soil, so unique to this part of the world that I haven't smelt it anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 我至今还能闻到那种空气，那是松树、轻木和潮湿泥土的混合气味，是世界这片地区所独有的，我在其他任何地方都没有闻到过。

sentences.en: But as beautiful as the city was when Luis was a kid, back in the 1980s, Medellín was also in the middle of a full-blown crisis.
sentences.zh: 但正如路易斯小时候这座城市那么美丽一样，在20世纪80年代，麦德林也正处于全面危机的中心。

sentences.en: 30 years ago, this was the murder capital of the world.
sentences.zh: 30年前，这里是世界的谋杀之都。

sentences.en: Today in Medellín, military police were patrolling the streets looking for bombers.
sentences.zh: 今天在麦德林，军警正在街头巡逻搜寻炸弹袭击者。

sentences.en: That's largely because of Pablo Escobar's notorious Medellín cartel, which waged a bloody drug war right on the city's streets.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是因为巴勃罗·埃斯科瓦尔臭名昭著的麦德林贩毒集团，他们在城市街道上挑起了血腥的毒品战争。

sentences.en: Thirteen bombs have gone off in Medellín since the weekend.
sentences.zh: 自周末以来，麦德林已经发生了十三起爆炸。

sentences.en: The city's mayor today signed an order imposing a 10 p.m.
sentences.zh: 该市市长今天签署了一项命令，从晚上10点起实行宵禁

sentences.en: to dawn curfew in the city.
At the time, my father was a captain in the counter-narcotics unit for Colombia's National Police.
sentences.zh: 当时，我父亲是哥伦比亚国家警察缉毒局的一名上尉。

sentences.en: He was basically fighting the narcos.
sentences.zh: 他基本上就是在跟毒贩作战。

sentences.en: I remember one day, when our family was leaving the city and my dad was driving our SUV, we were suddenly attacked and shot at.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一天，我们全家正要离开城市，我爸爸开着我们的SUV，我们突然遭到袭击和枪击。

sentences.en: My mom, brother, and I had to duck under the seats as my father sped away.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈、弟弟和我不得不躲在座椅底下，我父亲则加速驶离。

sentences.en: Escobar had declared war on the Colombian state.
sentences.zh: 埃斯科瓦尔向哥伦比亚国家宣战了。

sentences.en: My family eventually decided to leave the country, and we moved to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的家人最终决定离开这个国家，我们搬到了美国。

sentences.en: For Medellín's residents, the threat of random deadly shootings and bombings was real and constant.
sentences.zh: 对于麦德林的居民来说，遭遇随机致命枪击和爆炸的威胁是真实而持续的。

sentences.en: To outsiders, the city became synonymous with the cocaine war and indiscriminate violence.
sentences.zh: 对外人来说，这座城市成了可卡因战争和无差别暴力的代名词。

sentences.en: But then, in its darkest hour, Medellín began to find its way out of that crisis.
sentences.zh: 但随后，在最黑暗的时刻，麦德林开始寻找摆脱危机的方法。

sentences.en: I did a story a few years ago for this show about a sweeping revival program Medellín launched in the mid-1990s.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我为这个节目做过一篇报道，讲的是麦德林在20世纪90年代中期发起的一项意义深远的复兴计划。

sentences.en: As part of that plan, the city built parks and libraries and public spaces.
sentences.zh: 作为该计划的一部分，这座城市修建了公园、图书馆和公共空间。

sentences.en: Medellín's leaders also invested in poor neighborhoods, locally known as comunas.
sentences.zh: 麦德林领导层还投资了贫困社区，当地人称之为“康纳斯”（comunas）。

sentences.en: Community programs were created for residents who had long been neglected.
sentences.zh: 为长期被忽视的居民设立了社区项目。

sentences.en: The sweeping program was called social urbanism, a term coined by city leaders.
sentences.zh: 这项影响深远的计划被称为“社会城市化”，这是城市领导人创造的一个词。

sentences.en: It was designed to breathe new life into Medellín by investing in the needs of city residents.
sentences.zh: 它旨在通过投资城市居民的需求，为麦德林注入新的活力。

sentences.en: Social urbanism, along with a harder focus by police on drug trafficking,
sentences.zh: 社会城市化，再加上警方对毒品走私的更严厉打击，

sentences.en: helped the city's murder rate plummet by at least 80%.
sentences.zh: 帮助该市的谋杀率骤降了至少80%。

sentences.en: Against incredible odds, Medellín transformed from a notoriously violent narco capital
sentences.zh: 在不可思议的逆境中，麦德林从一个臭名昭著的暴力贩毒之都

sentences.en: to a more peaceful model city.
sentences.zh: 转型为一个更加和平的模范城市。

sentences.en: The press called it the Medellín miracle.
sentences.zh: 媒体称之为“麦德林奇迹”。

sentences.en: Today, celebrities who could live anywhere in the world have chosen to stay in Medellín, their hometown.
sentences.zh: 今天，那些本可以住在世界任何地方的名人选择留在他们的家乡麦德林。

sentences.en: That includes reggaeton stars like Jay Balvin.
sentences.zh: 其中包括雷鬼巨星杰·巴尔文等。

sentences.en: It's a city inside of the mountains.
sentences.zh: 这是一座藏在大山里的城市。

sentences.en: You know, it's a lot of nature around.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，周围有大自然。

sentences.en: I guarantee that you'll be back.
If not, I'll give you your money back.
sentences.zh: 如果没有，我把钱退给你。

sentences.en: In 2020, I decided to move back to Medellín.
I rented an apartment that I really liked from a friend in El Poblado,
sentences.zh: 我在埃尔波布拉多（El Poblado）从一个朋友那里租了一间我很喜欢的公寓，

sentences.en: not far from where my family had once lived.
sentences.zh: 离我家人以前住过的地方不远。

sentences.en: And now, I was close to all the best bars and restaurants.
sentences.zh: 现在，我离所有最好的酒吧和餐馆都很近。

sentences.en: Walking around, I sensed a city overflowing with creativity.
sentences.zh: 四处走走，我感觉到这座城市洋溢着创造力。

sentences.en: I discovered hip new design shops,
sentences.zh: 我发现了崭新时髦的设计店，

sentences.en: a listening bar where DJs played vinyl records every night,
sentences.zh: 一家DJ每晚播放黑胶唱片的聆听酒吧，

sentences.en: and my favorite cafe, where I often did work.
sentences.zh: 还有我最喜欢的咖啡馆，我经常在那里工作。

sentences.en: It really felt like the place to be.
sentences.zh: 真的感觉这里就是该来的地方。

sentences.en: But soon after I moved back, I started talking to other people in the city.
sentences.zh: 但自我搬回来后不久，我开始跟城里的其他人交谈。

sentences.en: And it became clear to me that Medellín is in trouble again.
sentences.zh: 我清楚地意识到，麦德林又陷入麻烦了。

sentences.en: Because in the last few years, there's been an explosion of new problems,
sentences.zh: 因为在过去的几年里，新问题呈爆炸式增长，

sentences.en: like huge spikes in housing costs,
sentences.zh: 比如住房成本的大幅飙升，

sentences.en: the widespread displacement of locals, and worse.
sentences.zh: 当地人广泛被迫流离失所，以及更糟糕的情况。

sentences.en: Many residents are now worried that the so-called Medellín miracle is crumbling.
sentences.zh: 许多居民现在担心，所谓的“麦德林奇迹”正在崩溃。

sentences.en: And they fear that their city is at another breaking point.
sentences.zh: 他们担心自己的城市正处于另一个崩溃点。

sentences.en: But before we get to the story of this latest crisis,
sentences.zh: 但在我们讲述这场最新危机的故事之前，

sentences.en: a quick reminder of what things were like
sentences.zh: 简单回顾一下当年的情况

sentences.en: when the Medellín miracle first started back in the mid-1990s.
sentences.zh: 20世纪90年代中期“麦德林奇迹”刚开始的时候。

sentences.en: At the time, residents were filled with hope about the future of their city,
sentences.zh: 当时，由于新的复兴计划，居民们对城市未来充满希望。

sentences.en: thanks to the new revival program.
People were especially excited about their brand new public transportation system.
sentences.zh: 人们对他们崭新的公共交通系统感到特别兴奋。

sentences.en: The Medellín Metro first opened in 1995.
sentences.zh: 麦德林地铁于1995年首次开通。

sentences.en: I remember the TV ads with aerial shots overlooking downtown,
sentences.zh: 我还记得电视上的广告，俯瞰市中心的航拍镜头，

sentences.en: showing the brand new trains with green and gold stripes speeding in and out of stations.
sentences.zh: 展示着带有绿金条纹的全新列车在车站进进出出。

sentences.en: I was eight years old when we went as a family to ride it for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我们全家第一次去坐的时候我八岁。

sentences.en: My cousin, brother, and even my grandma came.
sentences.zh: 我的表弟、弟弟甚至我奶奶都去了。

sentences.en: I remember looking out the train's window,

sentences.zh: 几乎就像在城市上空漂浮，

sentences.en: and getting a panoramic view of Medellín's skyline.
sentences.zh: 麦德林的天际线一览无遗。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people in Medellín felt this way.
sentences.zh: 我想麦德林的很多人都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: It was the first metro system in the whole country.
sentences.zh: 这是整个国家的第一个地铁系统。

sentences.en: It was proof that things could change.
sentences.zh: 这是事情可以改变的证明。

sentences.en: And maybe those really scary times were over.
sentences.zh: 也许那些真正可怕的时代已经过去了。

sentences.zh: 麦德林的居民开始感受到同样的乐观浪潮。

sentences.zh: 一直延伸到近330英尺的山麓。

sentences.en: It was created primarily as transportation for commuters
sentences.zh: 它的修建主要是为了方便通勤者，

sentences.en: in the working-class hillside neighborhood called Comuna 13.
sentences.zh: 位于被称为13号街区（Comuna 13）的工人阶级山坡社区。

sentences.en: The city also added more metro stations and cable cars going up into the comunas.
sentences.zh: 这座城市还增设了更多地铁站和通往各个社区的缆车。

sentences.en: El metro comienza a romper esa segregación como un elemento de transformación
